c.tagline: Bermuda's pastel harbour capital of Front Street shops and pink-sand beaches.

taxi.fareNote: Bermuda has no Uber or ride-hailing and does not allow visitors to rent cars. Getting around is by metered taxi (fixed government rates), the pink public buses, the Sea Express ferries, or a rented electric minicar or scooter.

emergency.note: 911 is the single emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance across Bermuda.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.St. George's (East End): St. Peter's Church St George's Bermuda

avoid.reason: Use care in the 'back of town' area north of Court Street late at night, where occasional street crime occurs.

hood_desc: Bermuda's compact pastel capital along Front Street, packed with harbourside restaurants, shops, and the island's ferry and bus terminals; the most convenient, walkable base and nightlife hub.
A leafy upscale parish just south of Hamilton fronting Elbow Beach and the eastern South Shore; a relaxed base of resorts and cottage colonies with easy beach access.
The island's southwest, home to Horseshoe Bay and a string of Bermuda's most famous pink-sand beaches plus its biggest resorts; ideal for a beach-focused stay.
A UNESCO World Heritage town at the East End - Bermuda's original 1612 capital, with narrow lanes, St. Peter's Church, and colonial forts; steeped in history.
A green central parish with the Crystal & Fantasy Caves, the Bermuda Aquarium at Flatts Village, and the sheltered Flatts Inlet; quiet and family-friendly.

water.note: Rain-collected tap water is generally safe; bottled is widely available if you prefer.

transit.pay: Buses and ferries share zone-based fares; buy paper tickets, tokens, or a multi-day transportation pass at the Hamilton bus and ferry terminals, or pay exact cash on board buses (no change given). A 1-3 day pass covers unlimited bus and ferry travel.
transit.hours: Pink buses run roughly 7am-11pm with reduced Sunday and holiday service; ferries run mainly daytime and early evening and less often in winter. There is little late-night transit, so taxis fill the gap.
transit.note: Visitors cannot rent cars in Bermuda; the pink public buses, the Sea Express ferries across the Great Sound, taxis, and rented electric minicars or scooters are how everyone gets around.

bus: Bermuda Public Transportation Board (island-wide pink bus network)
ferry: Sea Express ferries (Hamilton, Paget/Warwick, Dockyard, and seasonal St. George's routes)

car.idp: Not applicable - visitors may not rent cars; electric minicars and scooters are the rental option

transit.m: Taxi to City of Hamilton (20-30 min)
Public bus Route 1, 3, 10 or 11 to Hamilton (45-60 min)

tip.r: A 15-17% service charge (the 'gratuity') is typically added to hotel and restaurant bills; otherwise 15-20% is standard for taxis and dining.
